title: WIC: from eligibility to groceries — claim ledger

latest_comparable_release_check.finding: CY2023 listed as latest available; released December 2025.

editorial_method: Synthesis of published primary research and program guidance. No original interviews. Illustrations and rule demonstrations are labeled. National reach, local experiences, and redemption have different denominators and are not combined into an attrition funnel.

claims.claim: WIC provides supplemental foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and health care referrals to eligible population groups.
claims.limitation: Eligibility includes categorical, residency, income, and nutrition-risk requirements; packages differ by life stage.

claims.geography: United States, including territories in national estimate
claims.limitation: Modeled eligibility with administrative participation. Not unique annual people, rejected applicants, or a causal estimate of barriers.

claims.claim: Coverage increased from 53.5% in 2022 to 56.1% in 2023.
claims.denominator: Estimated eligible population in each year
claims.limitation: Does not establish the cause of the increase. CY2023 is the latest comparable eligibility-and-reach release found, not a claim that no later caseload figures exist.

claims.claim: Coverage: infants 82.3%; age one 67.4%; age two 52.5%; age three 45.2%; age four 26.9%.
claims.denominator: Estimated eligible people within each age group
claims.limitation: Different age groups, not a tracked cohort. Does not measure dropout, reasons for nonparticipation, or lifetime receipt.

claims.claim: Participants described eligibility misconceptions and competing responsibilities; others described convenient enrollment and assistance. Staff described retention outreach.
claims.denominator: 10 WIC participants; 17 clinical providers/staff; 6 WIC staff
claims.limitation: Small qualitative sample, not national frequency. Different accounts are not merged into one biography. Direct quote: “I had so many other things to put first.”

claims.claim: Large white eggs can qualify; brown eggs are not authorized. Qualifying cage-free eggs are authorized. State rationale is cost containment.
claims.period: Shopping Guide FAQs, revised April 2026, pp. 5–6
claims.denominator: Illustration of a four-year-old child with egg benefits available
claims.limitation: Generic cartons are not verified product SKUs. Approval requires approved product/package and sufficient issued benefits. No actual rejected transaction, national rule, or full-package value is claimed.

claims.claim: Caregivers described WIC product restrictions, shopping inconvenience, and stigma.
claims.geography: Two pediatric clinics in West Philadelphia
claims.limitation: Not nationally representative. The study’s SNAP-specific enrollment and recertification findings are not attributed to WIC.

claims.claim: At least 70% of the issued food benefit was redeemed in 69.6% of produce periods and 67.1% of egg periods.
claims.denominator: Certification periods with category issued: produce 365,738; eggs 364,908. Study includes 188,368 participants, with repeated periods.
claims.calculation: Produce 254,506 / 365,738; eggs 244,775 / 364,908. Published rounded percentages shown.
claims.limitation: Threshold attainment across periods, not share of dollars spent nationally. Lower redemption associated with discontinuation; no causal claim. Discontinuation means no issuance for two months after certification; continuing eligibility not established.

claims.claim: Electronic benefits associated with 9.12% relative increase in participation among children ages 1–4 three years after implementation; 95% CI 3.19–15.39%.
claims.denominator: Difference-in-differences comparison of EBT and non-EBT states
claims.limitation: Relative change, not percentage points. Not randomized; other state changes may contribute. Separate from national 2023 coverage trend; an evaluated past reform.

claims.claim: Same seven-item basket costs $22.63. With sufficient issued benefits, WIC pays $19.14 and the household pays $3.49 for soap.
claims.period: Retailer prices observed September 20, 2026; California rules April 2026
claims.denominator: One illustrative grocery purchase for an eligible child age four, not a full monthly package
claims.calculation: 429+199+399+299+399+189+349 = 2263 cents. Six food items = 1914 cents; nonfood soap = 349 cents.
claims.limitation: Assumes approved products and enough issued benefits. Single-gallon milk price, not multi-buy price. Retailer pickup prices illustrate in-store WIC payment, not online acceptance. Brown eggs are only a comparison and do not enter the receipts. Not actual household testimony or typical savings.

claims.claim: State tiles, eligible counts, participant counts, and 95% coverage intervals reproduce USDA Table 3.5.
claims.denominator: Estimated eligible people in each jurisdiction, all WIC categories
claims.limitation: Not a causal policy ranking. Differences reflect population composition and other conditions as well as policy. Geography-specific uncertainty is displayed.

claims.claim: 23.3% did not know about WIC; 22.6% thought they did not qualify.
claims.denominator: Current adult participants asked why they had not enrolled during prior pregnancies
claims.limitation: Not all currently eligible nonparticipants, not reasons attributable to the 2023 gap; historical self-report.

claims.claim: 59% of 125 former participants interviewed reported feeling they no longer needed WIC.
claims.limitation: Not nationally representative; does not establish ongoing eligibility.

claims.claim: Caregivers described food fit, cultural preferences, product mislabeling and checkout embarrassment, alongside benefits of EBT and apps.
claims.denominator: 37 interviews: 20 current caregivers, 17 early-leaving while eligible
claims.limitation: Themes are not prevalence estimates or measured explanations of the California redemption findings.

claims.claim: Larger basket total $42.97, WIC food value $39.48, household cost $3.49. Same unit prices as original basket, milk/apples/peas quantities tripled.
claims.geography: Illustrative California child age 4; Smart & Final store 522 price snapshot
claims.limitation: Regular unit prices, no volume discounts/taxes/fees. Assumes matching approved products, enough issued benefits and selected package options. Illustrative repetition requires continued eligibility, new monthly issuance, same prices. Not a typical monthly value or full food package.
